newsitem.title: UK: Labour's lead slips in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: Labour's lead slips in latest poll.

text.p: The British opposition Labour Party's opinion poll lead ahead of May 1 elections has dipped by four points in the past week, but voters are turning to the minority Liberal Democrats rather than the ruling Conservatives, a new poll showed.

The NOP poll for the Sunday Times, put support for Labour at 48 percent, down four points from a week ago, while support for Prime Minister John Major's Conservative Party was unchanged at 28 percent.
The Liberal Democrats were at 17 percent, up five points from last week and at their best NOP rating since May 1996.
The poll followed an apparent policy switch by Labour when it announced last week that it now favoured some privatisation of state assets provided it was in the public interest.
It showed 33 percent of voters opposed Labour's new position on privatisation while 22 percent supported it.
However, 55 percent of voters were in favour of more privatisations -- which have been one of the key features of the Conservatives' 18 years in power.
NOP interviewed 1,595 adults across Britain on Friday.
